title: MACE-MP shared force field with material Mirror code (conservative toy mechanism screen)
hypothesis: For held-out synthetic material potentials generated by a shared rank-2 invariant radial basis, a compact Mirror material code on a shared potential can recover energy and force quality with lower serialized payload than independent material coefficients, while exactly preserving conservative forces; it must outperform byte-matched native low-rank and sparse-update controls to support Mirror-specific value.
physical_object: Shared pair-radial energy basis and shared material coefficient subspace
mirror_coordinate: Two-dimensional material coordinate m fitted from sparse energy/force calibration

development.selection_metric: held-out combined energy/force normalized RMSE; select radial basis width and code rank

paid_objects: sparse indices and residuals where used

success_gate: Fresh held-out material combined normalized RMSE <= 0.02, exact energy-gradient force consistency and rotation equivariance, >=25% actual payload savings versus independent material coefficients, and a quality/storage advantage over native low-rank and sparse-update controls.
failure_gate: Any physical-consistency violation; failure of quality or byte gate; or exact/native-control alias without a Mirror-specific quality/storage/compute advantage.
boundaries: Scoped synthetic radial-potential mechanism screen only; no official MACE-MP, MPTrj, PA297, or real material result is claimed.
The Mirror coordinate is compared with a mathematically matched native low-rank coefficient control.
Fresh worlds are generated only after this protocol is committed.
implementation_amendment_01: Before fresh access, development code review found delta coordinates were fit without subtracting shared base predictions. Corrected fitting to yc - Xc@base for Mirror and sparse residual controls; also corrected serialization to store every target scalar-gate alpha. No fresh world was opened before this correction.
